history.summary: HelmCharts now has a deterministic gate: `.kubecoder/project.yaml` (setup + test only, no config.yaml), pytest as an optional Poetry `test` group with poetry.lock regenerated, and a 24-test hermetic suite pinning today's behaviour of release.resolve() and discover_releases(), plus one read-only pass over the real configs/prd/ (all 51 stages discovered and resolved). `kc project test` is green and mutation-checked. No lint/build verbs declared: the repo has no ruff config and builds nothing locally.

P1's outcome holds: `kc project test` is green (24 tests, 0.12s) from a `.kubecoder/project.yaml` the run loop will pick as the gate, the lint/build sweep is a clean no-op, `poetry install --only main` stays pytest-free, and four mutations of the guards P2 must preserve each turned the intended test red. One blocking finding: the real-tree discovery test asserts that every on-disk prd stage directory is enumerated, which is the negation of R2/V02, so the gate goes red the moment slice 009 registers the first `reconciler: argo-cd` entry.

findings.summary: tests/test_prd_tree.py:27 asserts every on-disk prd stage directory is discovered — the negation of R2/V02 — so the gate this phase ships goes red on slice 009's first `reconciler: argo-cd` entry.

history.summary: F1 (blocking) reproduced and fixed: test_prd_tree.py's on-disk oracle asserted set equality with discover_releases(), which R2 is designed to falsify — with R2's skip applied and a reconciler: argo-cd entry registered the suite went 1 failed, 23 passed. The oracle now derives ownership from the tree (missing file and missing key both mean jenkins, D38) and is pinned by a hermetic test beside it; green under that same mutation and inert on today's tree. kc project test is green (25 tests), lint/build are the intended no-ops, and the done-record plus P2's real-tree bullet are updated.

Round 1's blocking F1 is resolved and witnessed: the real-tree oracle is now reconciler-aware, and re-running r1's repro (P2's discover_releases skip plus slice 009's argo-cd entry) is green where it previously failed. The fix commit introduces no new problems — two mutations confirm the new hermetic pin is not vacuous and that the real-tree test still catches an over-broad skip — and the gate I ran by hand (kc project test, 25 passed) is green with lint/build the intended no-op.

R1, R2 and R3 landed together: _RELEASE_KEYS gained the five Argo keys, resolve() stops at the top-level allowlist for a non-jenkins entry (no chart-existence trip, no _UPSTREAM_KEYS check, and upstream dropped from the record so all three entry shapes report a falsy chart), discover_releases skips such a stage by direct file read, and eight writing verbs refuse it while plan/output/config/wait still work. kc project test is green at 49 tests, mutation-checked; a real-tree smoke entry made `deploy config` exit 0 with chart_name: null and left discover_releases returning exactly the 51 jenkins-owned stages.
root: cexec iac poetry run pytest    [  OK  ]

R1, R2 and R3 land together with the mechanism the rulings settled: resolve() gates both the upstream: validation and the chart-existence trip on the reconciler, _UPSTREAM_KEYS is untouched, and discover_releases skips by direct file read. The two 'prove no breakage' claims hold structurally — gen_architecture's deploy template call sits after its falsy-chart_name skip, and only the refused terraform verbs reach a state-writing command. Both findings are advisory; nothing blocks the merge.

findings.summary: The refusal's stated ordering before apply_cluster_environment is untested — moving the guard after it leaves all 14 test_main_verbs.py tests green.
A `reconciler:` key written with an empty value parses to None, so the refusal message reads 'is deployed by None' and the `reconciler: str` annotation is false for that input.

history.summary: The local-chart path in resolve_helm_args.py now resolves through the resolved chart name at all three mis-keyed sites — get_chart_args' routing test plus get_helm_images' values.yaml read and templates/ walk — so a release whose `chart:` overrides its config directory name resolves locally instead of falling through to the upstream repo path. Four tests ride along (three routing cases with both paths stubbed, one hermetic get_helm_images assert), each site mutation-checked; `kc project test` is green at 53 tests. Provably inert today: the only `chart:` in the whole tree is configs/dev/_ci/prd/release.yaml's falsy `chart: null`.
root: cexec iac poetry run pytest    [  OK  ]

P3 lands its outcome completely: the routing test and both get_helm_images reads now key on the resolved chart_name, so the local-chart path no longer depends on the config directory name. I verified inertness independently (the only top-level `chart:` in the tree is `chart: null`) and mutation-checked all three sites individually — each is caught by a test on its own. One advisory finding: a third, unrecorded site in recommend_resources.py carries the same config-directory keying.

findings.summary: recommend_resources.py keys the chart source on the config directory name (:168-176, :185, :210) — a third instance of P3's mis-keying that the close-out's P3 entry omits, naming only the Groovy sibling.

history.summary: Every requirement (R1-R3) and every ruling in the plan is delivered by a landed phase, and each of the 16 surviving acceptance criteria has implementing work I can point at in the merged HelmCharts tree: P1 the gate (.kubecoder/project.yaml, optional `test` Poetry group, hermetic suite plus the real-tree pass), P2 the allowlist widening, the reconciler-aware resolve() short-circuit, the discover_releases skip and the 8/4 verb partition, P3 the get_chart_args mis-keying at all three sites. The rulings' harder edges are honoured rather than drifted past — `_UPSTREAM_KEYS` untouched, `config` never refusing, V11's typo guard genuinely absent, the P1 gate-durability limitation stated rather than overclaimed — and the three entry shapes design.md specifies are each pinned by a parametrised test. No done-record admits a leftover that a phase owed, and no phase depends on something nothing produced. The one item clearing the mechanical-residue exception — main.py's module docstring listing nine of its twelve verbs, in a file P2 already touched — I fixed and committed here (HelmCharts 3c9af98, suite still 53 passed) and struck from the close-out; the remaining close-out entries are out-of-scope defects in files this slice does not touch, or sub-bar leftovers, and stay there for the operator.

Reran kc project test (53 passed, hermetic) and re-verified all 16 surviving verification.json items with test-level and real-tree live-check evidence (a temporary reconciler: argo-cd entry added/removed under configs/prd/, confirming discover_releases' skip and deploy config's non-raising short-circuit against real data); confirmed poetry install --only main ships no pytest and that audit-prd-orphans/recommend-resources cannot break from this slice's changes. Pushed HelmCharts (5 commits) under the devlock pre-authorization and confirmed via the Jenkins API that IaC/HelmCharts build #5820 collected releases and skipped all 51 deploy stages, so the push reached prd's pipeline without touching prd; no Ansible-repo commit belongs to this slice, so nothing was pushed there. No role/playbook/Terraform module changed, so no operator deploy is owed. No finding cleared the generation bar.

Updated the argo-cd/ document set (design.md's registry + coexistence sections, D38, phases.md A.3/B.5, a new history.md section) and HelmCharts' CLAUDE.md + tools/deploy/README.md to the shape that shipped: the reconciler: key and its jenkins default, the eight-verb refusal set with the four inspection verbs kept, the reconciler-aware resolve() that replaced chart: null, the discovery skip, and the repo's new pytest gate. AnsibleSpecs/decisions.md, docs/runbooks/ and the Ansible repo needed nothing — no standing rule moved and no runbook names this behaviour; /work/Ansible has no commit for this slice. kc project test green in /work/HelmCharts (53 passed); committed on HelmCharts main and AnsibleSpecs main (specs files staged by name), neither pushed. No architecture-model nudge: nothing here adds a host, daemon or external identity to the Ansible model.
